titel: Episode 818 - The Interview Was Great. The Employee Wasn’t.

einzeiler: How to handle a new hire who aced the interview but struggles on the job.
kurzfassung: When a promising new hire underperforms, leaders must diagnose specific behaviors instead of making vague complaints. Coaching, clear expectations, and a structured performance runway help determine whether the employee can grow into the role. Ultimately, if performance does not improve, leaders must address the gap and refine their hiring process to test actual judgment rather than interview vocabulary.
stichpunkte: Interviews test controlled performance, whereas daily workplace realities reveal actual capability.
Avoid broad complaints and identify specific missing behaviors or unmet standards.
Investigate root causes through direct conversations before labeling someone a bad hire.
Do not quietly compensate for weak employees, as this damages team trust and morale.
Establish a clear performance runway with specific expectations and a reasonable timeline for improvement.
Potential has an expiration date and must eventually translate into actual performance.
Refine the interview process by asking situational questions that test judgment over vocabulary.

clips.text: Vague complaints about an employee failing to meet expectations are useless for improvement, requiring leaders to pinpoint exact missing behaviors instead.

clips.hook: Your team is always keeping score.
clips.text: Colleagues instantly notice when someone fails to pull their weight or when standards are lowered for a single person.
Leaders cannot indefinitely manage employees based purely on future hopes rather than current results.

clips.hook: Interviewing someone's vocabulary versus their judgment.
clips.text: Standard interview questions merely test a candidate's ability to use polished leadership buzzwords rather than how they handle high-pressure crises.

beschreibung:
What should leaders do when a promising new hire or manager fails to perform after a great interview? This episode explains how to diagnose performance gaps, coach struggling employees, improve hiring decisions, and recognize when potential needs to become performance.
